title: Epic 1 Task: Validate performance, touch reliability, and MVP exit criteria
description:
Run Epic 1 validation pass: repeated 5-wave runs, touch-first placement reliability in landscape safe areas, smoke + gameplay checks, and explicit verification that deferred systems were not partially implemented.

## Context
Final gate before closing Epic 1 and unblocking Epic 2.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Repeated runs show no runaway node growth. 2) Touch interactions are reliable in landscape layout. 3) Epic 1 acceptance checklist is documented and passed. 4) Deferred systems remain out of implementation scope.

title: Epic 1 Task: Add HUD wiring, SCRAP upgrade action, and safety checks
description:
Wire HUD to show wave, ENERGY, and SCRAP; implement one simple SCRAP-based mid-wave upgrade action for Scrapper identity; and add guardrails for input validity, action feedback, and runtime cleanup checks.

## Context
Bridges game feel and MVP identity while enforcing stability requirements.
acceptance_criteria: 1) HUD reflects wave, ENERGY, and SCRAP updates in real time. 2) One SCRAP upgrade action works mid-wave with clear constraints. 3) Invalid actions are handled without crashes. 4) Node lifecycle cleanup checks are instrumented for repeat runs.

title: Epic 1 Task: Integrate minimal Scrapper card loop and ENERGY budget
description:
Implement minimal card system for MVP: one Scrapper starter deck, draw/discard flow, per-wave ENERGY budget, two construct cards (Arrow Tower and Splash Tower) that call runtime placement APIs, and one maneuver card (Overdrive Target Tower) with temporary effect lifecycle.

## Context
Second implementation milestone; depends on stable runtime interfaces from task 1.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Starter deck and hand lifecycle are functional. 2) Construct cards spend ENERGY and place correct towers via runtime API. 3) Overdrive maneuver card applies temporary effect and expires correctly. 4) Card plays fail gracefully when ENERGY or target conditions are invalid.

title: Epic 1 Task: Build 5-wave runtime loop with enemies, towers, and win/lose flow
description:
Implement the playable real-time tower-defense runtime slice: level orchestration, wave sequencing to 5 waves, enemy spawn schedule, two enemy archetypes (normal and fast/weak), two tower archetypes (arrow and splash), targeting by furthest path progress, and explicit win/lose state transitions.

## Context
First implementation milestone for Epic 1. Establishes runtime loop prior to card orchestration.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Five waves run start-to-finish with deterministic progression. 2) Arrow and splash towers fire on valid targets using furthest-progress priority. 3) Normal and fast/weak enemies traverse path and resolve death/base-hit outcomes. 4) Game can end in victory or defeat with clear state transitions.
notes:
Implemented runtime loop foundations for Epic 1 Task 1: level orchestration with 5-wave plans, enemy path-follow progression, normal+fast enemy variants, arrow+splash tower variants with furthest-progress targeting, base HP/win/lose transitions, HUD wiring updates, and emulator quickstart launcher script (scripts/launch_mobile_preview.sh). Diagnostics for modified Godot files are clean. Local runtime execution pending due missing emulator/godot binaries in this environment.
Resolved runtime parse failures from emulator launch: removed GameManager class_name conflict with autoload, replaced GameConstants enum typing with preload-backed constants in game_manager/level script, relaxed fragile BaseEnemy/BaseTower compile-time typing, and switched enemy/tower variant inheritance to explicit script paths. Smoke suite now passes cleanly on Godot 4.3.
Completed runtime loop debug and stabilization: fixed Path2D/PathFollow movement issue, added curve validity guards/probe logging, and implemented visible projectile VFX for both Arrow and Splash towers. Smoke tests passing.

title: Epic 0 Task: Scaffold test harness and smoke test suite
description:
Create initial test harness strategy and implement smoke tests for project boot plus key scene/script loading. Establish conventions for where tests live, how they run locally, and what constitutes a blocking failure.

## Context
Provides confidence gate prior to Epic 1 gameplay development.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Test harness scaffold exists and is runnable locally. 2) Smoke tests cover boot + critical scene/script loading paths. 3) Test execution instructions are documented. 4) Baseline pass/fail criteria defined for Epic 0 exit.
notes: Implemented smoke-test harness: tests/smoke/smoke_runner.gd validates boot settings, GameManager autoload, critical script loads, and scene load+instantiate checks. Added scripts/run_smoke_tests.sh wrapper and docs/test_harness.md with execution instructions and explicit Epic 0 pass/fail gate. Updated docs/skeleton_checklist.md with test harness deliverables. Local syntax diagnostics are clean; runtime execution requires a local godot/godot4 binary.

title: Epic 0 Task: Define emulator and device-testing workflow
description:
Document and validate emulator/simulator workflow for day-to-day development testing. Includes Android emulator baseline profile, iOS simulator notes, Godot desktop touch emulation settings, and repeatable runbook steps for local verification.

## Context
Ensures rapid feedback loop for mobile behavior before physical device packaging.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Android emulator profile and startup checklist documented. 2) iOS simulator prerequisites and constraints documented. 3) Godot touch emulation settings verified and documented. 4) New contributor can execute the workflow end-to-end.
notes: Implemented emulator/device-testing workflow docs in docs/emulator_workflow.md with: Android baseline AVD profile and startup checklist, iOS simulator prerequisites/constraints, verified touch emulation setting from project.godot, and an end-to-end new contributor runbook + smoke checklist.

title: Epic 0 Task: Establish Godot project skeleton and baseline structure
description:
Create the initial repository skeleton and baseline project assets required by Epic 0. Includes canonical directories, placeholder scene/script files, autoload-ready common module stubs, and an explicit checklist for folder-level conventions.

## Context
First executable slice of Epic 0; unblocks environment and test-harness tasks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canonical folders exist and match agreed architecture. 2) Placeholder scenes/scripts are present for gameplay, towers, enemies, and ui. 3) Base common stubs support forthcoming autoload wiring. 4) Skeleton checklist is documented for contributors.
notes: Implemented baseline Godot project skeleton: canonical directories, placeholder gameplay/tower/enemy/ui scenes and typed scripts, autoload-ready common stubs (GameManager + constants), initial project.godot with landscape/mobile defaults, and docs/skeleton_checklist.md for contributor checklist.

title: Epic 1: Hybrid MVP vertical slice (5-wave real-time TD + minimal card layer)
description:
Deliver the complete Hybrid MVP slice for VoidGrit. MVP scope is fully in-scope here: (A) Runtime Tower Defense Core: landscape 1920x1080 target, Godot 4 Mobile (Forward+) renderer, fixed single level with Path2D track, 5-wave loop, 2 tower types (single-target arrow and AoE splash), 2 enemy types (normal and fast/weak), tower targeting by furthest progress, win/lose loop, touch-first placement UX with safe-area HUD. (B) Minimal Deck/Card Layer from day one: one playable character deck (Scrapper only), ENERGY-per-wave budget, starter hand/draw/discard loop, 2 construct cards (Arrow Tower, Splash Tower) that instantiate existing runtime towers, and 1 maneuver card (Overdrive Target Tower) that modifies an active tower briefly. (C) Economy and identity: SCRAP drops from enemies with one simple mid-wave upgrade action to preserve Scrapper identity without full deck complexity. (D) Technical quality gates: spawned runtime nodes are cleaned correctly, no runaway memory/node growth through full 5-wave runs, touch reliability and readable HUD in landscape safe areas. (E) Explicit deferrals outside this epic: Hacker/Zealot decks, relic loops, procedural node map/meta progression, deep tower-combination trees, advanced barrier/path-redirection meta.

## Context
Primary MVP delivery epic. Must remain constrained to avoid scope creep while proving the hybrid loop.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Playable start-to-finish 5-wave run exists and can be won/lost. 2) All three starter cards function correctly and consume ENERGY as designed. 3) Construct cards route through runtime placement APIs; maneuver card targets active tower and expires correctly. 4) Scrapper-only scope is enforced in MVP with SCRAP drop and one upgrade action. 5) Performance and cleanup checks pass for repeated runs without node leaks. 6) Scope boundaries are documented: deferred systems are not partially implemented.

title: Epic 0: Project skeleton, environment, emulator, and test foundation
description:
Establish the project skeleton and development environment so all subsequent gameplay epics are built on a reproducible, testable base. Scope includes: Godot 4 project bootstrap; canonical folder structure (common, scenes/gameplay, scenes/towers, scenes/enemies, scenes/ui, assets/audio, assets/fonts); base autoload wiring; coding conventions checklist; local dev environment setup instructions; mobile emulator/simulator configuration for daily testing (Android emulator baseline profile and iOS simulator notes); desktop touch emulation setup; baseline CI-ready test harness strategy; and first-pass smoke tests for scene loading and core script validation.

## Context
Precedes all gameplay implementation work. Locks toolchain and dev-test feedback loop to reduce integration risk.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Repository contains agreed skeleton directories and placeholder scenes/scripts for gameplay, towers, enemies, and ui. 2) Environment setup instructions are documented for Linux/macOS with exact Godot version and editor settings. 3) Emulator/simulator dev-testing workflow is documented and executable by a new contributor. 4) Test suite scaffold exists with at least smoke coverage for project boot and key scenes/scripts. 5) Done criteria for handoff to Epic 1 is explicit and met.

title: Epic 3: Phase-2 deck expansion and tower-modifier depth
description:
Expand from minimal card layer to deeper deckbuilding: larger Scrapper card pool, richer modifier cards, stronger tower-combo mechanics, and improved card-state UX while preserving runtime TD performance constraints.

## Context
Builds system depth after MVP has validated player loop and technical stability.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Expanded card pool implemented with clear archetype tags. 2) Modifier interactions on existing towers are robust and test-covered. 3) Card UX supports clear targeting, preview, and resolution states. 4) Runtime performance remains stable under expanded card interactions.

title: Epic 2: MVP polish, QA hardening, and first mobile playtest packaging
description:
Harden the MVP for external playtesting: tuning wave pacing, balancing card/tower numbers, improving HUD clarity, adding lightweight SFX placeholders, validating touch accuracy across aspect ratios, profiling frame-time and memory behavior, and preparing first Android package path for internal testing.

## Context
Starts after core MVP is feature-complete and focuses on reliability and player feedback readiness.
acceptance_criteria: 1) MVP balancing pass is documented with before/after tuning values. 2) Performance baseline captured on representative device/emulator profiles. 3) QA checklist passes for touch, UI safe area, and full-run stability. 4) Internal playtest package workflow is documented end-to-end.

title: Epic 4: Roguelike meta progression and additional character archetypes
description:
Implement long-term progression systems aligned with VoidGrit vision: procedural run structure, relic/meta systems, and addition of Hacker and Zealot archetype decks with differentiated mechanics.

## Context
Long-term roadmap epic after MVP and phase-2 systems are proven.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Multi-run progression loop exists with procedural structure and persistence decisions documented. 2) Hacker and Zealot are playable with distinct mechanics and constraints. 3) Meta/relic systems integrate without breaking core combat pacing. 4) Long-run balance and content gating strategy is documented.
